title.narrative: Area based general protection and GBV Responses for Displacement Affected IDP, Host and Returnees in Northwestern Zone of Tigray - Asgede, Laelay Koraro, Shire Endaslasie town, and Tahtay Adiyabo.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to enhance the protection of communities affected by displacement in the Northwestern Zone of Tigray. The focus geographic areas include Asgede (with sites in Adi Mahmameday, Hitsats, and Mayhanse), Laelay Koraro (site: Selekleka), Shire Endaslasie town (with sites at Fre Swuat, Hibret, Shire General, Gaba Weyane, and Tsehaye Schools), and Tahtay Adiyabo (sites: May Kuheli and Shimblilina) Woredas. NRC and IMC will utilize their specific expertise, with NRC implementing general protection measures and IMC concentrating on GBV response. ltbrgtIMC aims to ensure critical lifesaving GBV prevention, risk mitigation and response services, supporting clinical SRH services and MHPSS services for GBV survivors and at-risk women and girls. This will ensure continued access to quality GBV services through existing IMC WGSS in Shire/Fresewat, Adimehameday and Mayhansen. The project will integrate GBV response services into SRH within HFs in the locations of Selekleka, and MayKuheli by deploying response staff to provide quality GBV case management services for survivors of GBV. The project will deploy community mobilizers to disseminate critical lifesaving information about service availability and access. These community mobilisers will also play a key role in linking survivors and at-risk women and girls from Shire IDP sites of Taba Woyane, and Shire general, to existing WGSS in Shire (Fresewat and Adikentibay) for comprehensive GBV services. The programme also enhances referral pathways and capacity for GBV responses through coordination with the BoWSA, health bureau, and WLO, including Moms for Moms, New Millennium Women Empowerment, and Heal Our People, and other relevant service providers. IMC will strengthen the capacity of service providers to meet survivors’ holistic needs, whilst engaging communities to reduce stigma and promote GBV prevention and response. To mitigate the risk of GBV, the project plans to conduct a safety audit and provide emergency dignity kit support, access to clinical and specialized care. GBV survivors and individuals who experience psychological distress will have lifesaving access to clinical SRH and MHPSS services with intersectoral coordination. These services will be integrated through timely, cross-sectoral referrals with WGSS and the closest HFs, alongside trained MHPSS officers who will provide specialized mental health services and psychoeducation for moderate to severe cases. Capacity-building training will also be offered to GBV and WLO workers on trauma-informed care, identification and timely referral of mental health conditions, and responding to crisis, suicide, and self-harm behaviors.ltbrgtltbrgtNRC aims to implement activities to improve general protection of displacement affected communities in NW Zone of Tigray. NRC will conduct protection monitoring with the aim of identifying protection risks for the target community and violations of rights, including information on the locations and movement of newly-arrived IDPs and barriers to accessing services, which will contribute towards informed programming and advocacy. Secondly, NRC will establish protection desks in six IDP sites in with the aim of providing protection services, including vulnerability screening, capacity building, and awareness raising. NRC will provide cash-based intervention for the most vulnerable amongst the target community to minimize their exposure to protection risks and counter negative coping mechanisms.ltbrgtThe proposal also feeds into the areas-based approach in the allocation strategy. Under both general protection and GBV program, a number of capacity building activities are planned for local authorities, community leaders and organizations, with the aim of producing sustainable outcomes.ltbrgt Overall, the actions in this project are aligned with the allocation strategy and priorities of the Protection Cluster strategy, and the 2025 Priority Humanitarian Response and Critical Funding Gaps. ltbrgtlt/pgt ltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
